transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because I feel like I’m always running hot, you know? Like I can’t shut the motor off. And lately, that’s been getting me in trouble at the firehouse. Which is crazy because I love the firehouse. I've been there for, what, twelve years now? Yeah, twelve years. Started right after I got my associate's degree. My buddy Mike, he was the one who talked me into taking the EMT course. We used to go fishing down at the lake every weekend, and one time he just brings it up out of nowhere. We didn't catch anything that day, by the way. Just a bunch of snagged lines. I lost my favorite lure, actually. It was this green spinnerbait... anyway, yeah, I just can't seem to stop moving and it's causing issues at work.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or were more talkative or restless than usual?

Unusually energized? I mean, I'm always energized, like I said. But not like... I don't know, not like some weird spell or anything where I don't sleep. I sleep fine, usually. Well, mostly. Sometimes the alarm goes off at the station and it totally wrecks you for the rest of the night. Have you ever heard that alarm? It's like this blaring, soul-crushing klaxon. They installed a new system last year because the old one kept shorting out whenever it rained hard. We had this huge storm roll through, knocked out power to half the county, and our alarm just kept going off every ten minutes. It was a nightmare. My captain, Dave, he was so mad he actually threw his boot at the speaker. Dave's got a temper, but he's a good guy. He makes this incredible chili, too. Secret ingredient is cinnamon, believe it or not. But yeah, no, I don't really get those periods you're talking about. I'm just always kind of going a hundred miles an hour.
Do you find it hard to focus on tasks or get easily distracted, especially during activities that require sustained attention?

Yeah, definitely. It's... it's actually a big problem. Like, we have these morning briefings, right? Or when we're doing the new drone training—they just got us these crazy high-tech drones for search and rescue, thermal imaging, the whole nine yards. The controller looks like an Xbox controller but with a giant screen. Anyway, I’m usually locked in for the first, I don't know, two or three minutes? But then... I don't even know what happens. I'll realize I’ve just been staring at the map on the wall or watching a fly buzz around the fluorescent lights, and I didn’t catch half of what command just said. Which is bad, obviously. You don't want to be the guy asking where the staging area is when everyone else is already gearing up. My captain, Dave—the chili guy—he's been getting on my case about it. He actually pulled me aside last week and asked if my hearing was going. My hearing's perfect, by the way. I get it checked every year at the occupational health place. The nurse there, Brenda, she always remembers that I'm allergic to latex. It's a mild allergy, just gives me a rash, but still, nice of her to remember. But yeah, focusing on stuff like that? It's like my brain just switches the channel without asking me.
When you were a kid, did you have similar issues with staying focused or feeling restless, especially in school?

Yeah, actually. My mom says I was exactly like this back in grade school. She loves telling this story about how I was always out of my seat, just wandering around the classroom. I guess I used to just blurt out answers without raising my hand, too. And losing homework? Oh man, that was a daily thing. I'd get these notes sent home all the time, which drove her crazy because she always said I was bright enough to do the work, I just wouldn't do it. Or I'd do it and leave it on the kitchen counter. We had this awful yellow Formica counter back then. It was the nineties, so I guess that was in style, but looking back, it was hideous. My dad tried to replace it himself once and ended up cracking the new countertop right down the middle. He was so stubborn about not hiring a contractor. We ended up living with that crack for like five years. Dirt would always get stuck in it, and my mom would have to use a toothbrush to scrub it out. She bought this special pack of neon toothbrushes just for cleaning. I think she still uses them for the bathroom grout... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, school. Yeah, I was definitely restless back then, too. Always in trouble for it.
Do you often feel irritable or have trouble managing your emotions, especially in stressful situations?

Irritable? No, not really. I mean, the job is stressful, sure. You're running into burning buildings or dealing with multi-car pileups on the interstate. But I don't really get mad or lose my temper. If anything, I'm just always moving, always trying to get to the next thing. Stress just makes me want to do more, you know? Like last week, we had this massive brush fire out near the old quarry. The wind was whipping up, totally unpredictable. We were out there for fourteen hours straight. Fourteen hours! My boots were literally melting to the asphalt at one point. We had to call in mutual aid from three different counties. And the guy they sent from Mercer County—I think his name was Greg—he brought this huge cooler full of Gatorade, but it was all the blue kind. I hate the blue kind. It tastes like melted popsicles, but not in a good way. The lemon-lime is the only way to go, especially when you're sweating that much. Although, my wife started buying this organic coconut water stuff, says it's better for hydration. It tastes like dirty dishwater if you ask me. I tried putting it in the fridge to see if cold made it better, but it just made it cold dirty dishwater. Our fridge is acting up anyway, the ice maker keeps jamming. I tried fixing it with a butter knife and almost broke the whole dispenser... but yeah, no, I don't really get irritable. Just busy.
Do you often act on impulse or do things without really thinking them through?

Impulsive? I don't know, maybe a little? Like, I don't think I do crazy things without thinking, but I definitely jump into stuff pretty fast. Especially at the station. Like if someone says there's a project, I'm already grabbing tools before they finish explaining it. Last month, Dave was talking about building a new rack for the hoses, and I just went out and bought all the lumber on my way home. Treated pine, mostly. It was on sale at Home Depot. I love going to Home Depot, honestly. The smell of the sawdust when you walk in? It's the best. I could spend hours in the tool aisle just looking at the new drills. They have these brushless motors now that are supposed to last forever and the batteries charge in like twenty minutes. I actually bought one of those rapid chargers for my drill at home because I was trying to fix the deck stairs. The bottom step was totally rotted out. My dog, Buster—he's a golden retriever mix, huge goofball—he actually fell through it a little bit. He was fine, just scared him, but I figured I had to fix it right then. I ended up pulling up half the deck boards because I thought, hey, while I'm at it, might as well replace them all, right? My wife came home and the whole backyard looked like a construction zone. She wasn't thrilled. We had to eat dinner inside for a week because I didn't finish it. I still haven't stained it, actually. I bought the stain, it's sitting in the garage. Cedar tone, I think. Or maybe redwood? The cans look exactly the same. I should probably check on that... wait, what did you ask me? About doing things without thinking? Yeah, I guess I do kind of just jump into things sometimes.

Have you ever experienced times when your mood has been extremely elevated, unusually irritable, or you've felt like you were on top of the world for days at a time, even if your energy wasn't necessarily higher?

Elevated mood? Like, on top of the world for days? No, I don't think I've ever had anything like that. I mean, I feel good when things go right, sure, but not like, crazy high for days. Just normal good, you know? Like when we finally beat the other shift in the annual chili cook-off. That was a good day. We've been trying to beat Shift B for three years. They always bring this ridiculously spicy ghost pepper chili that nobody actually likes, but the judges always give them points for heat. It's ridiculous. This year, I made a smoked brisket chili. I stayed up all night smoking the brisket out in my driveway. The smoker I have is one of those offset barrel ones, really heavy duty. I got it at a garage sale for like fifty bucks, which was a total steal because they retail for at least four hundred. The guy selling it was moving to a condo in Florida and didn't have room for it. He also tried to sell me a set of golf clubs, but I don't really play golf. I tried it once, but I couldn't stand just standing around waiting to hit a little ball. I need more action, you know? Anyway, the brisket took about fourteen hours, but it was worth it. We smoked them. Shift B was so mad. But yeah, feeling on top of the world for days? No, nothing like that. Just regular good days.

When you're trying to focus on something important, like during a critical operation at the firehouse, do you find that your mind wanders or that you're unable to stay mentally engaged even when you know it's necessary?

Mind wandering? Yeah, definitely. Like, even when it's really important stuff. We do these morning briefings, or sometimes we have this new drone training—which is actually pretty cool, they got us these DJI drones with thermal imaging so we can spot hot spots on a roof without having to send a guy up there right away. The controllers look like big video game controllers. I used to play a ton of Xbox when I was younger. Halo, mostly. My buddy Mike and I would stay up until three in the morning playing split-screen. You can't really do split-screen anymore, everything is online. It's kind of a bummer, honestly. I miss just sitting on the couch with a buddy and a pizza. We'd always get pepperoni and jalapeño. Best combo. But yeah, during the briefings or the drone training, I'm totally locked in for the first couple of minutes. I'm looking right at the captain, taking it in. And then... I don't know, I just sort of drift. Next thing I know, I realize I've been staring at the map on the wall or the drone screen for who knows how long, and I didn't catch half of what command just said. I usually have to ask one of the other guys what the actual plan is while we're getting our gear on. Good thing Dave takes good notes. He's got this little waterproof notebook he keeps in his breast pocket. Rite in the Rain, I think it's called. The paper feels kind of waxy. I bought one once, but I lost the special pen you need to write on it, so it's just sitting in my locker... but yeah, focusing is tough, even when I know I need to.
